analysis: The PR change is documentation-only: docs/reference/protocol-messages.md head lines 198-215 add a 'Close codes and the reconnect wait' section. The two supplied units are BASE surrounding text, with no changed lines on the base side, and the patch excerpt is complete. It documents that the provider reads only the WebSocket close code (1012 selects serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff; any other code or no close frame uses ExponentialBackoff), that a session stable for stableSessionDuration resets the backoff, that the close reason is ignored, that older providers treat 1012 like any other close, and that every reconnect sends a fresh register. No code, key handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or billing behavior changes. Relevant boundary TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) and asset A-018 (serving availability) are touched only descriptively. Reconnect wait is chosen from coordinator-authored close codes, and the coordinator is trusted. Attestation and App Attest authorization still apply on each fresh register, so the doc states no weakened reconnect guarantee. The 1012 wait does not grow the backoff, but the claimed range and bound live in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, which was not supplied. An integration pass should confirm that the implementation bounds serviceRestartDelayRange and does not allow a thundering herd or a tight reconnect loop; this is an unverified implementation contract, not a documented regression. The base units cover the unchanged inference_request, prefix-cache (T-041), model-replace and autopilot descriptions, and none are modified. No threat-model assumption is invalidated, and no threat-model update is required beyond optionally noting reconnect pacing under TB-002.
